title: Why MOH's FY2025 operating expenditure came in $310 million below initial estimates
asked: Mr Gerald Giam asked what specific factors caused the $0.31 billion reduction in MOH's revised FY2025 operating expenditure against initial estimates, and how the Ministry squares lower-than-projected funding needs for public healthcare institutions with the care demands of an ageing population.
response: The $310 million reduction is about 1.6% of the initial $18.8 billion estimate, mainly from lower-than-expected increases in operating costs at the public healthcare clusters, and sits within an accepted margin of budget variance. MOH's operating expenditure is still rising: the revised FY2025 estimate of $18.49 billion is $1.63 billion, or 9.7%, higher than the actual FY2025 operating expenditure, and the estimated FY2026 figure is $20.04 billion. Asked for more detail, Ms Rahayu Mahzam said the net decrease covers many lines of reduction, including the timing of some decisions, with some decreases offsetting increases. She said it was not an issue of compromising care to patients, and that healthcare services continued to be delivered well.
